output.brief: The enrolment fall is mainly a yield problem, not an applicant problem. Applications, admits and grades all rose. The drop in the share of admits who enrolled sits almost entirely in the Dean's and Merit award tiers, whose awards were cut from $14,000 to $9,000 and from $9,000 to $5,000. Yield in those tiers fell from about 45% to about 32%. Presidential awards (unchanged) and no-award admits were roughly flat. Early-action admits, whose decisions were on time on the old system, lost yield by the same amount as regular-decision admits (about 7.5 points). So the slow regular-decision turnaround does not explain most of the fall, though it was real and probably cost some individual students. Missing documents are unproven. I am fairly confident (roughly 75–85%). Next steps: do not replace the Director on this basis. Take the scholarship schedule back to the finance committee with a modelled proposal to restore awards in the affected tiers before award letters go out. Also set a monthly decision-turnaround target. Hold off on the vendor rebuild until the transcript issue is checked.
